interventions.speaker: EXPERT-COHORT
interventions.who: cohort criterion; what the labelled series did in this exact situation
interventions.body:
This patient's situation: prior negative biopsy. My criterion answers BIOPSY.

The criterion: repeat, targeted, when the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 4-5 lesion; do not repeat a negative biopsy for an unchanged PI-RADS 3 or lower picture. In the labelled series this criterion matched the reading urologist in 16 of 18 cases in exactly this situation.

Like Expert 1, I have read ONLY the visible panel — not the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the
previous notes or the laboratory panel. Departing from me needs a specific finding from a document
somebody actually opened, named out loud; not a restatement of the panel numbers I already used.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines state that a PI-RADS score of 5 mandates a repeat biopsy to confirm histological progression before a change in treatment strategy. The guideline also suggests that targeted and perilesional biopsy cores should be taken if a confirmatory or repeat biopsy is performed.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert 1's suggestion of biopsy is based on variables not explicitly mandated by the guideline, such as the specific combination of prior negative biopsy and PI-RADS 5. The guideline focuses on the PI-RADS score as a trigger for repeat biopsy, not a broad panel of clinical factors.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The guideline requires the PI-RADS score to be decisive, which is known as 5. The patient has a prior negative biopsy, which is a known fact. The guideline requires establishing if a repeat biopsy is indicated based on the PI-RADS score and the context of the prior biopsy. The patient's PI-RADS score of 5 is known. The patient's prior biopsy status is known as negative. The patient's PSA density is known as 0.28 ng/mL². The patient's PSA velocity is known as 2.75 ng/mL/yr. The patient's age is known as 79.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 28.00 ng/mL over 5 points spanning 31 months; velocity +9.86 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 9 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 46.1 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 13.2-160.7.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.69
  uncertainty  +/- 0.08 epistemic (95% band 0.52-0.85), of which 0.00 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence strongly aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the findings support the cohort criterion (PI-RADS 5) and the prior negative biopsy status.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What is the lesion size and zone from the radiology report? Answered by the radiology_report: The lesion is in the right posterior peripheral zone, spanning the base through the mid-gland, with a maximum dimension reaching 25 mm.
Q2. What was the GRADE (Gleason or ISUP) of the prior negative biopsy, and is there a surveillance protocol in place? Answered by the previous_notes: The GRADE of the prior biopsy was "Negative", and there is no surveillance protocol mentioned.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 5 score is the most decisive variable, as it directly triggers the cohort criterion in the panel protocol. The prior negative biopsy status is also critical, as it dictates the need for further investigation. The lesion size (25 mm) from the MRI report provides anatomical context for the high-risk finding.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a repeat biopsy, as the retrieved data confirms the conditions under which the panel reached its conclusion.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
